quest.title: The Hymn of Tir Yazad
quest.description: You've managed to gather all the Great Songs of Khvarena regardless. Now, it is time to resolve the anomaly in the sky...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x350, Primogem x40, Mora x25000, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6

dialogues.speaker: Nasejuna
dialogues.text: Then I shall leave the matter of the Twin-Horned Chaplet to you. I have some leftover work to take care of.

dialogues.speaker: Nasejuna
dialogues.text: I believe that all people, no matter who they are, will submit to you and the Envoy's awesome glory.

dialogues.speaker: Nasejuna
dialogues.text: When we have each done what we must, let us meet at the campsite upon the Temir Mountains.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sorush's been pretty quiet since we left the ruined factory.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She used to keep talking on and on, so Paimon's not used to her being silent now.

choices.text: She must've been frightened quite badly.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Cheer up, Sorush! We've still got so many things to do!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: For instance, we need to perform... um, that rite with a name Paimon can't remember, and then fix the giant hole.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: After we're done, let's treat ourselves to something delicious for our hard work!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We can have... Um, Paimon doesn't know what Pari prefer for food...

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: ...Pari don't need to eat, Silly Floater.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: *sigh* To think I have fallen so low to require the Pale Floater's comfort, what a shame.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: I'd rather be sealed into the Gray Crystals right away or find myself a cavern to slumber undisturbed for eternity, till everyone I know ceases to exist.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon said Paimon's not a Pale Floater! But is there really such a cavern?

choices.text: Avoidance can't really solve the problem.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: At this point, I'm past caring!

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: How am I supposed to live with the sheer embarrassment of being fooled by Nasejuna?

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Anyway, now that you've collected all the Great Songs of Khvarena, you can go to Mihir or Rashnu if you want to solve the anomaly in the sky.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Whatever the case, please leave me alone and pretend you never heard the things I said.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, you did say a lot of weird stuff...

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Awwww, stop! Please stop!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, stop teasing her now! She's been traveling with us for so long, after all, and Paimon doesn't wanna see her quit halfway.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What's more, Sorush does have... some good qualities... like, um...

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: I saw you hesitating! *wail* Stop patronizing me!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yep yep! And haven't we been working hard to extinguish the Sign of Apaosha?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's all thanks to you that we've made it so far!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: How did it go again? Let Paimon think... Ah, "As long as you keep going, I believe that it will only be a matter of time before you become a truly great adventurer."

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Really? Do you genuinely mean to praise me?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Yes, as genuine as a friend could be.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Hehe, I knew I was great!

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Hehe, my motivation is back.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Now that the motivated Sorush is back, let's go find Zurvan, fix the giant hole, and get the reward! Paimon can't wait for her big meal!

choices.text: You've got a sense of responsibility.
There are still things you must do, right?

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: I know, I know, but...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Zurvan, we're back!

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: #Ah, it's {NICKNAME}, Sorush, and Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: By the looks of it, you must've obtained all the Great Songs of Khvarena.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: Whatever the case, the result is desirable. I was right to entrust the mission to you.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: Without you, the Great Songs of Khvarena might've been robbed away by those with ill intent.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, why does Paimon feel like Zurvan saw what was coming?

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: Eh-he, so I was on to something! You didn't run into the followers of the dark hollow, did you?

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: Well... Instead of dwelling on how I knew, why don't you tell me what exactly happened?

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You recount your adventure in the underground ruins and Nasejuna's betrayal to Zurvan.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: Hehe, even the Order's Vijnanapati had sided with the dark hollow. That was unexpected — not that I had any hopes in them to begin with, but that's just a step too far.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: And if I'm not mistaken, Nasejuna had been enticed into pursuing the Great Songs of Khvarena by the servant of the dark hollow you fought. That one's an old acquaintance of mine.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? You know that guy from the Abyss Order?

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: Hmph, he used to be with the Order of Skeptics. Several hundred years ago, an investigation team from the forest came to explore the secrets of the Dahrians.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: They insisted on entering the Dahrian ruins despite the Order's warning. So the then-Vijnanapati sent the man to go with the team in case something happened.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: No one knew what they encountered in the ruins, but by the time he reappeared, he had already embraced the defilement's blessings, and the investigation team was nowhere to be found.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: Then came the followers of the dark hollow. They were after the Great Songs of Khvarena and for that purpose, they summoned countless demons of Dev to attack the Vourukasha Oasis.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: Although we managed to protect our home with the help of many Pari and human warriors, we didn't eradicate the dark hollow's followers.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: To ensure that I left no gaps for them to exploit, I sealed the Vourukasha Oasis and the many ruins with the power of the Great Songs.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: The Order of Skeptics never recovered from this incident. They lost their ancient archives to fire, and gradually became like this.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: I sensed that the followers of the dark hollow were making their play since you last mentioned them, but I didn't expect them to have corrupted even the leader of the Skeptics.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, Paimon's still wondering about what Nasejuna said. Do you know anything about the Skeptics' ancestors?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You've fought alongside them, after all.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: Hehe, history becomes legend, legend becomes tale — that's how traditions live on. Forgetting is also part of the story.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: The more you cling to the idea of tradition, the more you only selectively remember the story you desire and eventually become lost in the maze of tales.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: In a world where things are being forgotten every hour of every day, what we engrave on the ground is far more reliable than what we sing to the wind.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: That's why I trust you, for you're forthright and never seem to concern yourselves with other people's judgment.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Although you're praising us, the way you put it sounds somewhat odd...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I somehow feel a sense of sarcasm.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: I presume Elder Zurvan's words are intended for me...

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: As for what happened five hundred years ago, I think you'd want to see for yourself than hear my version of the story.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: And now you have exactly the perfect opportunity.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: By the way, Sorush, it appears that you've grown more reliable now. With what you've been through, have you awakened from those raving-mad myths of humans?

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Elder! Please just let bygones be bygones!

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: #It seems that I made the right decision to entrust the issue to {NICKNAME} and Paimon. In that case, I guess I can also leave the Rite of Ab-Zohr in your capable hands without any reservations.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: The Rite of Ab-Zohr...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon remembers hearing Zurvan mention it! Is it for cleansing... um, defilement of sorts?

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: The Rite of Ab-Zohr is a ritual performed to cleanse the Harvisptokhm of defilement. Normally, you only need to conduct it under the trees that suppress darkness.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: However, with the seal weakening and the anomaly re-emerging in the sky, we need more than the usual to solve the problem.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: The anomaly appeared above the Harvisptokhm as a result of the tree absorbing a great amount of defilement.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: With that excessive amount of filth building up within it, and the corrosion caused by the anomaly, the Harvisptokhm can no longer sustain the Khvarena's power.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: The only thing we can do now is enter the Harvisptokhm to cleanse it and wake our god.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So we can actually enter the Harvisptokhm?

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: Of course. Did you think that the Rite of Chinvat was to be performed inside that dark hollow? Even Pari wouldn't be able to stand the defilement within.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: Inside the Harvisptokhm lies a giant lotus, Gaokerena, and our god's consciousness slumbers within it. By cleansing the defilement, the Flower of Sanctity will bloom once again.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: The Amrita will rid the land of all its impurities. Convoluted as these processes may sound, I believe they shall constitute no hindrance to you.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: Well then, I have already sent Rashnu and Mihir to the Tunigi Hollow. You need only bring over the Great Songs, and then you'll be able to gather the power of Khvarena.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: Khvarena will awaken the huge trees that are suppressing the darkness and purify the contaminated mud in the depths. After that, you can then perform the Rite of Chinvat and thus open the path into the Harvisptokhm.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: And once you are inside, the Chaplet will reveal to Sorush the great deeds of ancient heroes.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: Since all memories related to Khvarena will return to the Harvisptokhm in the end, these memories will never fade no matter how legends are retold and changed.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: I've never heard of this!

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: Hehe, the Chaplet was originally a part of the Harvisptokhm. You will know when you get there.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: Now, please go and extinguish the Sign of Apaosha. We will meet again when Amrita falls from the sky.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: Oh, then why don't you tell me what exactly happened?

dialogues.speaker: Rashnu
dialogues.text: What took Sorush so long...

dialogues.speaker: Mihir
dialogues.text: We've been waiting here for a very long time.

dialogues.speaker: Rashnu
dialogues.text: I'm so tired... I want to... go back to sleep. Zzz...

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Hey, that's not fair. I'm the one who's been laboring hard all along and you didn't do anything!

dialogues.speaker: Mihir
dialogues.text: That's not true. Waiting is also an important job. In fact, acting is only momentary while waiting is eternal.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's with this weird logic...

dialogues.speaker: Mihir
dialogues.text: That's just the philosophy of us Pari.

dialogues.speaker: Mihir
dialogues.text: But now is not the time to discuss philosophies. What matters is the Great Songs of Khvarena. I trust you've collected all of them, no?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Of course we have!

dialogues.speaker: Mihir
dialogues.text: In that case, let us remove the seal. Then you can gather the power of Khvarena with the Great Songs.

dialogues.speaker: Mihir
dialogues.text: But be careful. Since the filth has been building up for centuries, I have no idea what will emerge once I remove the seal.

talks.objective: Place the Great Song of Khvarena

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Now that we've placed the Great Khvarena properly, everything around here seems to have recovered!

dialogues.speaker: Mihir
dialogues.text: These trees were originally cultivated with Khvarena to resist the corrosion of the cataclysm. It's just that their power has ebbed away with the passage of time.

dialogues.speaker: Mihir
dialogues.text: With the Great Songs' nourishment, they will be able to regain their former glory.

dialogues.speaker: Mihir
dialogues.text: But with the seal removed now, the filth from the past has been freed, too.

dialogues.speaker: Mihir
dialogues.text: The rite won't be able to continue if Rashnu and I spend all our energy here. So please take care of these locations for us.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Hehe, leave it to me! It's the Bloomguard's job to fight defilement!

talks.objective: Place the rest of the Great Songs of Khvarena
Place the rest of the Great Songs of Khvarena
Place the rest of the Great Songs of Khvarena
Place the rest of the Great Songs of Khvarena

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mm, our work is done!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It seems that some flowers have grown on the tree. But what do we do next?

dialogues.speaker: Mihir
dialogues.text: Ah, don't look at me. I'm as clueless as you.

dialogues.speaker: Mihir
dialogues.text: Now that Sorush has already put on the Twin-Horned Chaplet, she can connect to the memories and wisdom of the Harvisptokhm using the Chaplet.

dialogues.speaker: Mihir
dialogues.text: Give it a try, Sorush.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: I know, but I'm not yet used to the Chaplet!

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Um... I think I see new shoots sprouting, but the filth hasn't been fully cleansed yet.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: We still need to purify these flowers.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Then the pure power of Khvarena will thrive again.

talks.objective: Go to the first huge tree
Go to the second huge tree
Defeat the monsters that have been released
Go to the third huge tree
Defeat the monsters that have been released

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's gotten quiet, finally.

dialogues.speaker: Mihir
dialogues.text: Now, perform the Rite of Chinvat before the filth starts to ooze out again.

dialogues.speaker: Mihir
dialogues.text: Then our job will be done.

dialogues.speaker: Rashnu
dialogues.text: And that means... I can sleep in peace... without anyone disturbing me.

dialogues.speaker: Mihir
dialogues.text: Come on, Sorush!

dialogues.speaker: Rashnu
dialogues.text: Sorush, hurry up!

dialogues.speaker: Mihir
dialogues.text: It has to be the three of us.

dialogues.speaker: Rashnu
dialogues.text: I'm so tired... I want to... go back to sleep. Zzz...

dialogues.speaker: Mihir
dialogues.text: Done. The path to the depths has opened, and our mission is completed.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, that was quick. You kept talking about "rite" and stuff, so Paimon thought it'd take a whole bunch of complicated incantations to conduct.

dialogues.speaker: Mihir
dialogues.text: Hmph, only humans need such things, as they can't even wield the power of the elements on their own.

dialogues.speaker: Mihir
dialogues.text: We Pari are different, for our power and that of the Khvarena hail from the same source. It's like how you humans don't need to recite incantations to walk.

dialogues.speaker: Mihir
dialogues.text: Um... Although you don't walk, you float.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Like Paimon said, your logic is weird.

dialogues.speaker: Mihir
dialogues.text: Anyway, let's not waste our time on this irrelevant topic. I'll leave what's next up to you.

dialogues.speaker: Mihir
dialogues.text: "May the eternal Khvarena guide us on the upward path."

dialogues.speaker: Mihir
dialogues.text: Whether it is Sorush or myself, all Pari have a duty that they must undertake.

dialogues.speaker: Mihir
dialogues.text: But you are different. You have come to help us out of the goodness of your hearts. For that, you have my thanks.

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: Then, please extinguish the Sign of Apaosha. You will know what transpired in the past once you're inside the Harvisptokhm.

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: We will meet again when Amrita falls from the sky.

dialogues.speaker: Mihir
dialogues.text: Whether it is Sorush or myself, all Pari have a duty that they must undertake.

dialogues.speaker: Mihir
dialogues.text: But you are different. You have come to help us out of the goodness of your hearts. For that, you have my thanks.

dialogues.speaker: Rashnu
dialogues.text: I'm so tired... I want to... go back to sleep. Zzz...

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: The Great Songs of Khvarena are, at their heart, comprised of past memories.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: The Sinless Seedlings shall have grown out by now.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You've gotten too far. Sorush can't continue purifying...
